marked: Morris (STOC 2005, math/0507307) proved the first polylogarithmic bound, O(log^44 n) for n a power of 2; Montenegro and Tetali improved it to O(log^29 n); Morris (Ann. Probab. 37 (2009) 453–477) proved O(log^4 n) for all even n, and O(log^3 n) for n a power of 2 (arXiv:0912.2759). Czumaj and Vöcking (ICALP 2014, LNCS, pp. 344–355) studied the shuffle through non-Markovian couplings [verify the bound obtained]. The order is not determined. Open.
correct_text: Morris, Improved mixing time bounds for the Thorp shuffle (arXiv:0912.2759), proves O(log³ n) when n is a power of two. Its Introduction records the earlier O(log⁴ n) bound without the power-of-two assumption and the previous log⁴⁴ and log²⁹ bounds. The unverified Czumaj–Vöcking citation is removed. The conjectured order is not established by this result. Open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.2759 ; abstract PDF p.1: 'the mixing time of the Thorp shuffle is O(log3 n)'; Introduction PDF p.2 specifies the earlier unrestricted O(log4 n) bound.

marked: Chen, Hu and Shi (arXiv:2108.05610) proved P(X_n > 0) = n^{−2+o(1)} at criticality, described by the authors as a weaker confirmation of the predictions. Chen, Dagard, Derrida, Hu, Lifshits and Shi (Ann. Probab. 49 (2021) 637–670, arXiv:1907.01601) confirmed the free-energy conjecture under an integrability condition, as reported in arXiv:2405.09741 [verify the precise form proved]. Exactly solvable relatives are treated by Hu, Mallein and Pain (arXiv:1811.08749, continuous time on a Yule tree) and by Alsmeyer, Hu and Mallein (arXiv:2502.02991, geometric Galton–Watson tree); the dual subcritical regime is in arXiv:2306.12717; Duquesne and Shi (arXiv:2609.11435) study the continuous Derrida–Retaux branching process, conjectured to be the scaling limit of the discrete model. The sharp asymptotics of Conjectures 1 and 2 remain unproved. Open.
correct_text: Chen, Hu and Shi (arXiv:2108.05610) prove critical survival n^(−2+o(1)). Chen, Dagard, Derrida, Hu, Lifshits and Shi (arXiv:1907.01601), Theorem 1.1, prove F_infinity(p)=exp(−(p−p_c)^(−1/2+o(1))) as p decreases to p_c under E[(X_0^*)³ m^(X_0^*)]<infinity for the paper's fixed positive-law initial distribution mixed with an atom at zero. This establishes the essential-singularity exponent, not an exact leading constant or the sharp critical survival asymptotic. Open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.01601 ; Theorem1.1 PDF p.3, integrability E[(X_0^*)³ m^(X_0^*)]<infinity and displayed free-energy formula. Section1 defines X_0^* and p mixture.

marked: Bramson (arXiv:1010.3142) proved stability of weighted max–min fair sharing for general interarrival and service distributions with 2 + δ moments. Massoulié (arXiv:0707.4542) treated proportional fairness with exponential-type assumptions [verify the scope]. Gromoll and Williams (Ann. Appl. Probab. 2009) established fluid limits. Paganini, Tang, Ferragut and Andrew (IEEE Trans. Automat. Control 57 (2012) 579–591) gave a Lyapunov function for the fluid model under smoothness assumptions, and Fu and Williams proved stability of subcritical fluid model solutions for general file sizes. Positive recurrence of the stochastic model for α-fair policies with general file sizes has not been established [verify whether later work completed this step]. Open.
correct_text: Bramson (arXiv:1010.3142) proves weighted max–min fairness stability for general interarrival and service distributions under moment assumptions. Massoulié (arXiv:0707.4542) proves proportional-fair stability with Markovian routing, covering phase-type service-time distributions; this is not a theorem for arbitrary file-size laws. General-distribution fluid-model results alone do not establish positive recurrence of every alpha-fair stochastic network. The general-distribution alpha-fair stability question remains open in the source formulation. Open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.4542 ; abstract PDF p.1: 'remains valid under so-called phase-type service time distributions'. This verifies the marked scope; a separate current-status search is recorded for the general open target.

marked: With α_0 = α_1 = 1 the model is the voter model, which clusters in d ≤ 2 and has a one-parameter family of extremal invariant laws in d ≥ 3. The dimensions covered by the conjecture are those in Neuhauser–Pacala's paper [verify; d ≥ 2 is the natural range]. Their Conjecture 2 asks that one type takes over on the other side of the coexistence region near (1, 1). The model is monotone when α_0 ∧ α_1 ≥ 1/2 (Cox–Durrett–Perkins, eq. (1.30), citing Proposition 8.1 of Cox–Perkins).
correct_text: Use d>=2 for the coexistence conjecture. Cox and Perkins explicitly describe the two-dimensional conjecture near (1,1), and record that their earlier Theorem 4 confirms the corresponding coexistence assertion for d>=3 near (1,1). At (alpha_0,alpha_1)=(1,1) the voter-model boundary behaviour differs between d=2 and d>=3. The present target is the conjectured coexistence region, not a claim for d=1.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.0158 ; PDF p.8: 'Neuhauser and Pacala have conjectured coexistence holds along the diagonal'; the same paragraph distinguishes d>=3 from d=2 and cites Conjecture 1 of Neuhauser–Pacala.

marked: Mytnik and Perkins (Probab. Theory Related Fields 149 (2011) 1–96) proved pathwise uniqueness for β > 3/4. Mueller, Mytnik and Perkins (Ann. Probab. 42 (2014) 2032–2112) gave non-uniqueness for non-elliptic coefficients with exponent below 3/4 [verify whether pathwise or in law]. Bass and Perkins proved uniqueness for elliptic coefficients 1/2 + ε-Hölder in an enhanced norm that does not cover pointwise coefficients. Han's generalized coupling method gave weak uniqueness for elliptic g with β > 3/4, and Han (arXiv:2608.01279) lowered this to β > 2/3. Open.
correct_text: For non-elliptic coefficients, Mueller, Mytnik and Perkins construct a nonzero solution of du=(1/2)Delta u dt+|u|^gamma dW with zero initial data when 0<gamma<3/4. Since the zero solution also exists, their example has nonuniqueness both in law and pathwise. This degenerate-noise counterexample does not settle the uniformly non-degenerate target in this row. The claimed type of nonuniqueness is confirmed.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2767 ; abstract, PDF p.1: 'neither unique in law nor pathwise unique'.

marked: Fav(K_n) → 0 by Besicovitch's projection theorem, since K is purely unrectifiable. A lower bound c/n follows from Mattila's capacity bound, and Nazarov, Peres and Volberg note that a random analogue has Fav comparable to 1/n while it is not clear whether the deterministic set decays at that rate. The natural conjecture is Fav(K_n) ≈ n^{−1} up to logarithmic factors [verify that this is stated as a conjecture in the literature]. Other self-similar sets (rational product Cantor sets, the Sierpinski gasket) raise the same question.
correct_text: The task is to determine the actual asymptotic decay of the Favard length of the deterministic four-corner approximants. The random analogue has a 1/n rate, but this does not establish the deterministic rate. Remove the unverified attribution of a conjecture asserting 1/n up to logarithmic factors; the opened Nazarov–Peres–Volberg abstract asks for the exact rate without asserting that prediction.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.2942 ; abstract PDF p.1 says the exact rate is an open problem. The deterministic and random constructions must be distinguished.

marked: Onsager's conjecture on energy conservation for Euler is resolved (Isett; Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol), and Bruè, Colombo, Crippa and De Lellis (arXiv:2212.08413) construct deterministic forcings for which forced 3D Navier–Stokes solutions dissipate anomalously, with Onsager-critical bounds. For stochastic forcing, the 4/5 law is proved conditionally on WAD (arXiv:1803.09695); the analogous laws are proved for passive scalars advected by stochastic Navier–Stokes (Bedrossian, Blumenthal and Punshon-Smith) and for stochastic Burgers (Gao and Kuksin, arXiv:2209.14288 [verify]), and Hofmanová, Pappalettera, Zhu and Zhu (arXiv:2305.08090) obtain anomalous dissipation of a passive scalar. WAD itself has not been established for any non-degenerate stochastic forcing. Open.
correct_text: Gao and Kuksin prove weak and strong versions of the Kolmogorov 4/5-law for the space-periodic one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation. The source is arXiv:2209.14288, revised August 2023; this is a Burgers result, not a proof of anomalous dissipation for stationary three-dimensional Navier–Stokes solutions.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.14288 ; PDF p.1, title and abstract, identifies Peng Gao and Sergei Kuksin and the one-dimensional Burgers equation.

marked: On regular trees Angel and Holroyd showed that the i.i.d. uniform configuration has escape rate 1/b on the b-ary tree for b ≥ 3 and is recurrent for b = 2. Florescu, Levine and Peres (arXiv:1408.5533) proved that the range of any rotor walk on a periodic Eulerian graph in R^d is at least of order t^{d/(d+1)}, and used the mirror model and critical percolation to prove recurrence with i.i.d. uniform rotors on the Manhattan lattice and the F-lattice. Kaiser and Sava-Huss (arXiv:2210.00810) proved recurrence on the Sierpinski gasket graph; Huss and Sava-Huss (arXiv:1805.05746, 1805.11983) studied range and speed on trees. No result is known for Z^d with d ≥ 2 [verify]. Open.
correct_text: Florescu, Levine and Peres (arXiv:1408.5533) prove recurrence of the uniform rotor walk on the Manhattan lattice and F-lattice, using planar mirror/percolation arguments. Their Introduction identifies recurrence on the ordinary square lattice as a difficult unresolved problem. Kaiser and Sava-Huss (arXiv:2210.00810) treat the doubly infinite Sierpiński gasket. These state spaces are distinct from ordinary Z^d; remove the overly broad assertion that no result of any kind is known for Z^d. The standard-lattice recurrence/transience target remains open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.5533 ; Introduction PDF p.2 and Theorem1.5. https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.00810 ; Introduction, Our contribution, identifies the gasket state space.

marked: Esfandiari et al. obtained 1 − 1/e. Azar, Chiplunkar and Kaplan, and Correa, Saona and Ziliotto improved this, the latter showing that blind strategies cannot exceed 0.675. Harb (arXiv:2307.00971) obtained 0.672, and Chen, Huang, Li and Tang (arXiv:2411.01191) obtained 0.688 with a non-blind algorithm. On the hardness side Bubna and Chiplunkar (arXiv:2211.04145) showed 0.7254, and Giambartolomei et al. obtained 0.723 as cited by Chen et al. [verify whether a later bound improves 0.723]. Open.
correct_text: Chen, Huang, Li and Tang (arXiv:2411.01191) give a 0.688-competitive algorithm and cite the 0.723 impossibility bound of Giambartolomei et al. Their Introduction reports the earlier 0.672 algorithm. These numbers are attributed to this inspected source rather than asserted to be an exhaustively certified latest bound. The newest-first prophet-secretary title search through 15 October 2026 located no later improvement claim; it also found the different competition-complexity problem. The exact optimal competitive ratio remains open.

marked: Peres and Solomyak proved Fav(K_n) ≤ C exp(−a log* n). Nazarov, Peres and Volberg (arXiv:0801.2942) proved Fav(K_n) ≤ C n^{−1/6+δ}. Bateman and Volberg improved the lower bound to c log n / n [verify]. Łaba and Zhai (arXiv:0902.0964), Bond, Łaba and Volberg (arXiv:1109.1031) and Łaba and Marshall (arXiv:2202.07555) extended power-law bounds to rational product Cantor sets, and Marshall (arXiv:2509.02882) obtained N^{−1/5+u} for the four-corner set. Random variants have exact rates (arXiv:2609.33557). The gap between log n / n and n^{−1/5} remains. Open.
correct_text: Bateman and Volberg prove Fav(K_n)>=c log(n)/n for every n, Theorem1 of arXiv:0807.2953. Marshall, arXiv:2509.02882v2 (August 2026), proves the four-corner upper bound N^(−1/5+u) for every u>0. Thus the lower bound has a logarithmic improvement over c/n, while the exact deterministic rate remains undetermined. Open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.2953 ; Theorem1 PDF p.3, display(1.2). https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02882 ; abstract PDF p.1 explicitly states the four-corner N^(−1/5+u) bound.

marked: The order of magnitude (log T)^{k²} is known in several ranges: Radziwiłł and Soundararajan, and Heap and Soundararajan, proved matching lower bounds for all k > 0; under the Riemann hypothesis Harper proved the sharp upper bound for all k > 0; unconditionally Heap, Radziwiłł and Soundararajan proved the sharp upper bound for 0 ≤ k ≤ 1 [verify each range]. The asymptotic with the conjectured constant is known only for k = 1 and k = 2 (with lower-order terms for k = 2). Moments of moments over short intervals were studied by Bailey and Keating (arXiv:2006.04503). Open.
correct_text: Heap and Soundararajan, arXiv:2007.13154, Theorem1, prove lower bounds of order T(log T)^(k²) for every fixed real k>0. Harper, arXiv:1305.4618, Theorem1, proves the matching upper bound under RH for every fixed k>=0. Unconditionally, Heap, Radziwiłł and Soundararajan, arXiv:1901.08423, Theorem1, prove the sharp upper bound for 0<=k<=2, not merely 0<=k<=1. Order-of-magnitude bounds do not supply the Keating–Snaith leading constant. Open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13154 ; Theorem1 PDF p.1 and Corollary1 p.2. https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.08423 ; Theorem1 PDF p.2, range 0<=k<=2. https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.4618 ; Theorem1 PDF p.1.

marked: For joint eigenfunctions of the Laplacian and the Hecke operators on arithmetic surfaces, Lindenstrauss (Ann. of Math. 163 (2006) 165–219) proved arithmetic QUE, completed for the modular surface by Soundararajan's escape-of-mass bound (Ann. of Math. 172 (2010)); Brooks and Lindenstrauss (Invent. Math. 2014) need only one Hecke operator [verify]. Without arithmetic structure, Anantharaman (Ann. of Math. 168 (2008)) showed every semiclassical measure has positive entropy, Anantharaman and Nonnenmacher (math-ph/0610019) at least half the maximal entropy in constant curvature, Dyatlov and Jin (arXiv:1705.05019) that semiclassical measures on hyperbolic surfaces have full support, and Dyatlov, Jin and Nonnenmacher (arXiv:1906.08923) the same for surfaces of variable negative curvature. Uniqueness of the semiclassical measure is not known for any compact negatively curved manifold without arithmetic symmetry. Open.
correct_text: Brooks and Lindenstrauss prove QUE for suitable joint quasimodes of the Laplacian and one Hecke operator on compact congruence surfaces. In particular, exact simultaneous eigenfunctions of the Laplacian and this single Hecke operator fall within the result; the entire Hecke algebra is not required. This arithmetic hypothesis does not establish QUE for all eigenfunctions on an arbitrary compact negatively curved manifold. Open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.5311 ; abstract PDF p.1: 'the Laplacian and one Hecke operator on compact congruence surfaces'; Theorem1.1 gives the joint-quasimode assumptions.

marked: Babai and Seress (1988) proved exp((1 + o(1))√(n log n)); Helfgott and Seress (Ann. of Math. 179 (2014) 611–658, arXiv:1109.3550) proved the quasipolynomial bound exp(O((log n)^4 log log n)). For two random generators the diameter is polynomial with high probability (Babai and Hetyei; Schlage-Puchta; Helfgott, Seress and Zuk give O(n²(log n)^c) [verify]). Keevash and Lifshitz (arXiv:2307.15030) obtain essentially sharp diameter estimates for generating sets of density at least exponential in −n. Computations of Chervov, Fedoriaka, Konstantinova and Naumov (arXiv:2509.19162) suggest that the largest diameters for two generators are of order n²/2. No polynomial bound is known for general generating sets. Open.
correct_text: Helfgott, Seress and Żuk prove that two independent uniform permutations generate a Cayley graph of their generated group with diameter O(n²(log n)^c), with probability tending to one; c is absolute. Thus the marked random-generator bound is correct, but it is not a worst-case bound for every generating set. The general polynomial-diameter conjecture remains open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.6742 ; abstract PDF p.1 and Theorem1.1, explicitly S={g,h,g^(−1),h^(−1)} and G=<S>.

marked: Coherence-based arguments, which bound inner products of pairs of columns, cannot give k beyond order √m: this is the square-root bottleneck. The problem is a derandomisation question for a high-dimensional probabilistic property, closely related to bounding clique numbers of Paley-type graphs; certifying RIP of a given matrix is NP-hard (Bandeira, Dobriban, Mixon and Sawin, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 59 (2013) [verify]).
correct_text: Coherence arguments face the square-root bottleneck. The construction question seeks deterministic analogues of a property random matrices have with high probability. Certifying whether an arbitrary input matrix satisfies a specified restricted isometry property is NP-hard, as proved by Bandeira, Dobriban, Mixon and Sawin; this certification hardness is distinct from constructing a special family with a proved guarantee.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.1580 ; abstract and Problem2 PDF p.1: testing whether a matrix satisfies RIP is NP-hard. Publisher metadata DOI10.1109/TIT.2013.2248414 confirms IEEE Transactions on Information Theory59(6)(2013),3448–3450.

marked: Möbius disjointness is known for many classes: rotations (Davenport), nilsystems (Green–Tao), horocycle flows (Bourgain–Sarnak–Ziegler), and various classes of interval exchange transformations and rank-one systems surveyed in arXiv:1710.04039 [verify each attribution]. Matomäki and Radziwiłł's theorem on multiplicative functions in short intervals gave the averaged form of two-point Chowla (Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Tao); Tao proved the logarithmic two-point Chowla conjecture and the equivalence of logarithmic Chowla and logarithmic Sarnak; Tao and Teräväinen proved logarithmic Chowla for odd order; Frantzikinakis and Host proved the logarithmic Sarnak conjecture for zero-entropy systems with countably many ergodic invariant measures [verify]. The conjecture in its original Cesàro form remains open in general. Open.
correct_text: Frantzikinakis and Host prove logarithmic Möbius disjointness for every zero-topological-entropy system with at most countably many ergodic invariant measures: for every continuous g and every starting point y, (log N)^(−1)sum_(n<=N) g(R^n y)mu(n)/n tends to zero. Their Theorem1.1 includes uniquely ergodic zero-entropy systems. This is a logarithmically weighted theorem and does not establish the original Cesàro-averaged Sarnak conjecture for all zero-entropy systems. The unverified list of separate historical attributions is replaced by this precise inspected theorem. Open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.00677 ; Theorem1.1, PDF p.2, exact entropy, countability, observable and starting-point quantifiers. The original conjecture is stated in the abstract and Introduction.

marked: Bourgain, Dilworth, Ford, Konyagin and Kutzarova (Duke 2011) gave the only unconditional construction beating the bottleneck, with k = m^{1/2+ε_0} for a very small ε_0, later increased slightly by Mixon [verify]. Bandeira, Fickus, Mixon and Wong (arXiv:1202.1234) conjectured that Paley equiangular tight frames are RIP; Bandeira, Mixon and Moreira obtained a construction conditional on a clique-number bound for Paley graphs [verify], and Satake and Gu (arXiv:2010.11179) one conditional on the generalized Paley graph conjecture. No unconditional deterministic construction reaches k = m^{1/2+γ} for moderate γ. Open.
correct_text: Bandeira, Fickus, Mixon and Wong's opened survey, arXiv:1202.1234, Section3, describes Bourgain et al.'s deterministic RIP construction at sparsity M^(1/2+epsilon) for a small positive epsilon. Its Paley-frame discussion conjectures random-matrix-like RIP and relates it to Paley clique estimates. The unverified later improvement and conditional-construction attributions are removed rather than assigned an unchecked bound. The much stronger deterministic construction target is not supplied by these results. Open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.1234 ; Section3 opening, PDF p.6: sparsity K of order M^(1/2+epsilon); abstract and Paley-frame section formulate the remaining conjecture.

marked: Kiss, Manolescu and Sidoravicius (Ann. Probab. 2015) analysed planar forest fires near the critical time; van den Berg, Kiss and Nolin proved deconcentration and mesoscopic clusters for volume-frozen percolation; van den Berg and Nolin (arXiv:2210.05642) proved the fire-lane statement for the volume-threshold model and (arXiv:2407.13652) studied fires ignited from the boundary. The infinite-volume Drossel–Schwabl process for fixed ζ exists (Dürre) [verify], but its ζ → 0 behaviour beyond the critical time is not understood. Open.
correct_text: For every fixed ignition rate lambda>0, the infinite-volume forest-fire model on Z^d, d>=2, admits a stationary translation-invariant distribution, as proved by Stahl, arXiv:1203.5533, Theorem1. This gives a directly inspected fixed-rate existence result; it does not resolve the small-ignition-rate fire-lane geometry asked in the row. Van den Berg and Nolin's arXiv:2210.05642 concerns the related volume-threshold model. Open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.5533 ; Theorem1 PDF p.3, fixed lambda>0 and d>=2. Dürre's original existence-paper metadata is papers/meta_durre.json, DOI10.1214/ejp.v11-333; the attempted original PDF returned an access-block page and was not treated as inspected theorem text.

marked: Algorithms exist for restricted classes: bipartite expanders and unbalanced bounded-degree bipartite graphs via cluster expansions and Markov chains (Jenssen, Keevash and Perkins; Liao, Lin, Lu and Mao; Chen, Galanis, Štefankovič and Vigoda; Cannon and Perkins) [verify list]. Cai, Galanis, Goldberg, Guo, Jerrum, Štefankovič and Vigoda proved #BIS-hardness for antiferromagnetic two-spin systems on bounded-degree bipartite graphs in the non-uniqueness region [verify]. Neither an FPRAS nor NP-hardness is known for #BIS. Open.
correct_text: Jenssen, Keevash and Perkins give an FPTAS and efficient sampling for the high-fugacity hard-core model on bounded-degree bipartite expander graphs; this verifies a restricted-class algorithm, not an algorithm for all bipartite graphs. Cai, Galanis, Goldberg, Guo, Jerrum, Štefankovič and Vigoda prove #BIS-equivalence for antiferromagnetic two-spin parameters beta*gamma<1 in the tree nonuniqueness region, with the exception beta=gamma and lambda=1. That zero-field symmetric exceptional case has an FPRAS, so the original blanket nonuniqueness claim needs this qualification. The unchecked longer algorithm-author list is removed. General #BIS remains open.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.04804 ; abstract PDF p.1, high-fugacity bipartite-expander hypotheses. https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.4451 ; Theorem2 and its following sentence, explicitly excludes beta=gamma,lambda=1 and records its FPRAS.

marked: Montgomery (1973) proved the conjecture for test functions with Fourier support in (−1, 1) under the Riemann hypothesis. Rudnick and Sarnak (Duke Math. J. 81 (1996)) proved the analogous result for all n-level correlations with restricted support; Goldston and Montgomery related the conjecture to primes in short intervals; Odlyzko's computations of zeros near the 10^20-th and later zeros agree closely with the GUE prediction [verify]. Goldston, Lee, Schettler and Suriajaya (arXiv:2503.15449) showed that the conjecture implies that almost all zeros are simple and on the critical line. No extension of the support beyond (−1, 1) is known. Open.
correct_text: Odlyzko's computations include almost176million zeros near the 10^20-th zero and over101million near zero number2×10^20. Here10^20 denotes the zero index, not its imaginary height. His Introduction describes the tested spacing statistics through Montgomery's pair correlation and random-Hermitian-matrix predictions, and reports excellent agreement in most cases. Goldston, Lee, Schettler and Suriajaya (arXiv:2503.15449) prove that their vertically formulated PCC implies that asymptotically100% of zeros are simple and lie on the critical line, without assuming RH. This implication does not prove PCC. Open.
source: https://www.dtc.umn.edu/~odlyzko/unpublished/zeta.10to20.1992.pdf ; Chapter1, printed pp.1–2 (PDF pp.4–5), inspected as rendered images because the embedded text encoding is unreadable. Quotes: 'zeros near the 10^20-th zero were computed'; 'the agreement between conjectures and empirical data was excellent in most cases'. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.15449 ; abstract PDF p.1.
